notes: A fresh install now starts with a different three stations, and with the schedule set to turn the radio off when the day's last slot ends rather than carrying the last station on indefinitely. Play on launch stays off, with the station at the top of the list chosen. None of this touches an existing install: stored settings are merged over the defaults, so stations, order, theme and schedule all survive an update. Saving no longer stops to ask about a missing frequency. It is read out of the station's own name where it is there -- NewsTalk 1010, KISS 92.5 -- and anything left over is an internet-only station, which is filled in as Web stream with a button to correct it. A stream that has been retired is now recognised. BBC World Service serves a valid playlist listing one variant that has answered 410 Gone since it was withdrawn, and the app reconnected forever. Each quality is checked before it is played; when none are there the radio says the stream is gone, lights a steady amber, and stops trying. A name that only just overflows its box now drifts across at nine pixels a second instead of lurching a few pixels and snapping back. The Settings panel opens and closes on one curve per direction rather than two that finished at different times. Deleting a station no longer offers to move its slots somewhere else -- they go with it. The station finder has a magnifier for an icon and its city list is no longer clipped off after two suggestions. And holding Shift on Settings - Service reveals a button that copies the app folder's path and opens it.
